content.hero_subtitle: Create secure Apache .htpasswd entries for HTTP Basic Authentication
content.p1: The htpasswd tool generates password entries for Apache HTTP Server's basic authentication (.htpasswd files). These files contain username:password pairs that protect web directories, admin panels, staging sites, and development environments behind HTTP Basic Authentication.
content.what_desc: A .htpasswd file stores usernames and hashed passwords used by Apache's mod_auth_basic module. When a user tries to access a protected directory, Apache prompts for credentials and verifies them against this file. The passwords are never stored in plain text.

features.fast: bcrypt ($2y$): Most secure option with adaptive cost factor. Recommended for all new setups
features.fixed: APR1 MD5 ($apr1$): Apache-specific MD5 variant. Good compatibility with older Apache versions
features.deterministic: SHA-1 ({SHA}): Base64-encoded SHA-1 hash. Simple but offers basic security
features.support: crypt(): Traditional Unix DES-based encryption. Maximum 8-character password support

uses.verify: Admin Panels: Protect WordPress wp-admin, phpMyAdmin, or custom admin areas
uses.checksum: Staging Sites: Keep development and staging environments private
uses.cache: API Endpoints: Add basic authentication layer to REST APIs
uses.integrity: Static Files: Restrict access to sensitive documents and downloads

content.warning_desc: Always use bcrypt for new htpasswd entries. APR1 and SHA-1 are supported for backward compatibility but are weaker. Never transmit .htpasswd files over unencrypted connections. Always pair HTTP Basic Auth with HTTPS.

faq.q1: How do I use the generated htpasswd entry?
faq.a1: Create a .htpasswd file in a directory outside your web root and paste the generated entry. Then add AuthType Basic, AuthName, AuthUserFile, and Require valid-user directives to your .htaccess or Apache config.
faq.a2: Always choose bcrypt for new setups. It's the most secure option with an adaptive cost factor that makes brute-force attacks extremely slow. Use APR1 only if your Apache version doesn't support bcrypt (pre-2.4).
faq.q3: Can I have multiple users in one .htpasswd file?
faq.a3: Yes. Add one username:password entry per line. Each user can use a different algorithm. Apache will check credentials against all entries in the file.
